# Sensor Controller Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The sensor controller is the interface between analog sensor alert events and the standard alert reporting path. It receives alert indications from the analog sensor top and converts them into alert requests for the alert receiver. It also provides software with configuration, status, and test capabilities.

The module behaves as a set of independent alert channels. Each channel corresponds to one physical or environmental sensor alert class: active shield, clock glitch detector, voltage glitch detector, high temperature sensor, low temperature sensor, light sensor, and miscellaneous “other” alert.

## 2. Operating Conditions

- The module is synchronous to a single system clock and uses an active-low reset.
- Software accesses the module through a TL-UL slave interface.
- The alert output path uses the standard OpenTitan alert sender protocol.
- The alert sender path may be configured at build time to support asynchronous operation with the alert receiver. In that mode, the alert receiver is not required to share the module’s clock domain.

## 3. Sensor Alert Event Detection

Each sensor alert is presented as a pair of level signals: a positive line and a negative line. The normal deasserted state of a channel is positive low and negative high. The normal asserted state is positive high and negative low.

The module shall treat a channel as active when:

- the positive and negative lines are in the normal asserted state, or
- the pair is in any state other than the normal deasserted state.

This means that a stuck-at fault on either line must not be able to hide a real alert event. Invalid differential states, including both lines high or both lines low, shall be treated as active alert conditions. Each channel shall be evaluated independently.

## 4. Alert Request and Acknowledge Behavior

For every active alert channel, the module shall assert the corresponding alert request to the alert receiver. The request shall remain asserted until the condition that caused it is removed.

The module shall also provide a sensor-source acknowledge for each channel. The sensor-source acknowledge shall be a pulse and shall be generated according to the selected acknowledge mode.

### 4.1 Immediate Acknowledge Mode

In immediate acknowledge mode:

- A valid sensor alert event shall cause the alert request to be asserted without requiring software intervention.
- The event shall not be latched into the software-visible alert state.
- When the alert receiver acknowledges the request, the module shall generate a sensor-source acknowledge for that channel.
- The alert request shall stay active while the sensor event remains active. If the sensor source continues to assert the event after being acknowledged, the module shall continue to report it.

### 4.2 Software Acknowledge Mode

In software acknowledge mode:

- A valid sensor alert event shall set the software-visible alert state for that channel.
- The alert request shall be asserted while the latched alert state is set.
- The alert receiver acknowledge shall not, by itself, cause a sensor-source acknowledge.
- The module shall wait for software to clear the latched alert state.
- When software clears the latched state, the module shall generate a sensor-source acknowledge and remove the alert request.
- If the sensor event is still active after the software clear, the module shall treat it as a new event and may set the latched state again.

The acknowledge mode shall be selectable independently for each alert channel.

## 5. Software-Visible Functions

### 5.1 Alert State

For each alert channel, software shall be able to read the current latched alert state. In software acknowledge mode, a set bit indicates an unacknowledged sensor alert event. Software clears the bit to acknowledge the event. In immediate acknowledge mode, the latched alert state is not used for alert forwarding.

### 5.2 IO Power Status

The module shall continuously sample the IO power-OK status from the analog sensor top and present it in a read-only status register. This status shall always be updated and shall not be affected by alert events or acknowledge mode.

### 5.3 Alert Test Requests

Software shall be able to issue an alert test request for each channel. A test request shall exercise the alert request path without requiring the sensor source to produce an event. Test requests are independent per channel.

A test request shall not, by itself, set the software-visible alert state. It is intended only to verify the alert reporting path.

### 5.4 Sensor-Source Trigger

The module shall provide a software-writable trigger value to the analog sensor top. The trigger outputs shall follow the value written by software and are independent of the alert request path. These triggers are intended to cause the sensor source to generate test alert events.

## 6. Reset Behavior

When reset is asserted, the module shall:

- clear all software-visible register state,
- deassert all software-driven test and trigger outputs,
- return all configurable acknowledge modes to their default values,
- deassert all alert requests and sensor-source acknowledges.

After reset is released, the module shall respond to active sensor alert events according to the configured acknowledge mode.

## 7. Register Access

The TL-UL register interface shall provide access to all software-visible state described above. Write access to read-only fields shall be ignored. Software shall be able to read the current status, read and clear alert state, select acknowledge modes, and issue test requests and sensor-source triggers through this interface.
